lines: At 4.95%, a $400,000 mortgage paid off over 300 months costs $2,315.05 a month. At 4.7% (−0.25 pt) it would be $2,258.58: −$56.47 a month, −$677.64 a year.

If your payment stays fixed while the rate moves (common with Canadian variable mortgages), the payment doesn't change; instead about $81.70 a month less goes to interest, and the rest to paying down the balance.
This works out your numbers under the change you gave. It doesn't say whether rates will change; that's for each central bank and lender to decide.
data.follows: Variable-rate mortgages in Canada move with the lender's prime rate, which follows the Bank of Canada's policy rate, usually by the same amount within a day or two of a decision.
assumptions: Interest compounded twice a year (how Canadian lenders state mortgage rates), paid monthly, rounded to the cent.
The rate stays at 4.7% for the rest of the 300 months.

meta.notice: Educational information, not investment advice. ATLAS Explain never tells anyone to trade.
credit: Arithmetic on the numbers given; a reference rate names its source
